Chapter 1 — Project Introduction & Problem Solved

1.1 What is SupportDesk? (SupportDesk क्या है?)

Concept Definition (अवधारणा परिभाषा)
English: SupportDesk is an enterprise-grade IT Help Desk and Support Ticket Management System built with Java 17 LTS, Spring Boot 4, Spring Security, Spring Data JPA, and MySQL. It enables corporate employees to submit technical support requests, allows IT administrators to assign tickets to specialized technicians, enforces strict priority-based Service Level Agreements (SLAs), and maintains an immutable chronological activity history for transparency and compliance.
Hinglish: SupportDesk एक एंटरप्राइज आईटी हेल्प डेस्क और सपोर्ट टिकट प्रबंधन वेब एप्लिकेशन है जिसे जावा 17, स्प्रिंग बूट, स्प्रिंग सिक्योरिटी और MySQL पर बनाया गया है। इसमें कंपनी के कर्मचारी अपनी तकनीकी समस्याएं (जैसे लैपटॉप ख़राब होना, वीपीएन एरर) दर्ज करते हैं। एडमिन इन टिकट्स को तकनीशियनों को सौंपते हैं, और सिस्टम स्वचालित रूप से SLA समय-सीमा की निगरानी करता है ताकि कोई भी समस्या बिना समाधान के अटकी न रहे।
Real-Life Workplace Example (वास्तविक कार्यस्थल उदाहरण):
Imagine an office without a help desk: When an employee's laptop screen fails or SAP software crashes, they send an email to the IT group or walk over to IT desk. The email gets lost in someone's inbox, no technician takes ownership, the manager has no visibility, and three days later the employee is still blocked. With SupportDesk, the employee logs in, creates a ticket (`TCK-20261014-E02BCC`), selects "CRITICAL" priority, and the system immediately calculates a 4-hour SLA deadline. The admin assigns it to a technician, the technician resolves it, notes the fix, and the entire audit history is preserved in MySQL.

1.2 Who Uses SupportDesk? (इसके उपयोगकर्ता कौन हैं?)

The platform defines three strictly segregated user personas governed by Spring Security Role-Based Access Control (RBAC):

Role Primary Responsibilities System Permissions
EMPLOYEE General corporate staff reporting hardware, software, network, or access issues. Can create tickets for themselves, view only their own ticket history, and post comments on their tickets. Forbidden from viewing other employees' tickets or accessing admin dashboards.
TECHNICIAN IT engineers and hardware/software specialists resolving assigned tasks. Can view all assigned tickets, update ticket lifecycle statuses (`IN_PROGRESS`, `RESOLVED`), submit resolution notes, post technical comments, and access the technician workload dashboard.
ADMIN IT Managers, Operations Leads, and System Administrators. Complete administrative authority: register and manage employee accounts, assign tickets to technicians, view executive analytics dashboards, generate date-range reports, and monitor SLA breaches.

1.3 How to Pitch This Project in Interviews (इंटरव्यू में प्रोजेक्ट कैसे समझाएं?)

Interviewers frequently ask: "Can you introduce your project in 30 seconds or 2 minutes?" Use these proven scripts:

The 30-Second Elevator Pitch (30 सेकंड का त्वरित परिचय) Interview Ready
"I built SupportDesk, a full-stack IT service management platform engineered with Java 17 and Spring Boot. It streamlines workplace technical support by replacing chaotic email chains with structured ticket lifecycles, automated 4-tier SLA tracking, and role-based access control. The backend features stateless JWT authentication with token revocation on password change, clean layered architecture, and an automated test suite of 185 tests with zero failures."
Hinglish Explanation: "मैंने SupportDesk बनाया है, जो जावा 17 और स्प्रिंग बूट पर आधारित एक आईटी हेल्प डेस्क सिस्टम है। यह ऑफिस में ईमेल की अराजकता को ख़त्म करके टिकट्स का सुव्यवस्थित जीवनचक्र, 4-स्तरीय SLA ट्रैकिंग और रोल-बेस्ड एक्सेस कंट्रोल (RBAC) प्रदान करता है। सुरक्षा के लिए स्टेटलेस JWT और पासवर्ड बदलने पर टोकन इनवैलिडेशन लागू किया गया है, और इसे 185 ऑटोमेटेड टेस्ट्स के ज़रिए प्रमाणित किया गया है।"
The 3-Minute Comprehensive Technical Overview (3 मिनट का गहन तकनीकी विवरण) Architecture Focused
"SupportDesk solves the core operational challenge of tracking enterprise IT requests against rigid Service Level Agreements. On the backend, I implemented a Spring Boot 4 REST API utilizing Spring Data JPA and Hibernate for persistence against MySQL. Security is enforced through Spring Security with stateless JWTs. To prevent stolen token persistence, I devised an HMAC-SHA256 password fingerprinting mechanism in `JwtUtil` that immediately revokes tokens if the employee's password changes, requiring zero database schema alterations.

The business core in `TicketService` automatically calculates resolution deadlines across four priority tiers—from 4 hours for Critical down to 48 hours for Low priority. It tracks overdue status dynamically using index-optimized JPQL queries. Every state transition triggers an audit log in `ticket_activities` and dispatches in-app notifications.

On the client side, I built a responsive vanilla JavaScript Single-Page Application that manages authentication tokens purely in closure memory to protect against XSS and persistent storage theft. The application handles exceptions globally with `@RestControllerAdvice`, sanitizing error outputs to prevent SQL or stack trace leakage. I verified the entire application using MockMvc and JUnit 5 across 185 unit and integration tests."
Hinglish Explanation: "इस विवरण में आप आर्किटेक्चर, सिक्योरिटी, बिजनेस लॉजिक और टेस्टिंग चारों मुख्य स्तंभों को कवर करते हैं। इंटरव्यूअर को स्पष्ट समझ आता है कि आपने सिर्फ ट्यूटोरियल फॉलो नहीं किया, बल्कि वास्तविक प्रोडक्शन सुरक्षा (जैसे HMAC फिंगरप्रिंट से टोकन अमान्य करना, SQL इंजेक्शन से बचाव, XSS से सुरक्षा के लिए इन-मेमोरी टोकन) और डेटाबेस ऑप्टिमाइज़ेशन को गहराई से समझा है।"

2.1 The Verified Technology Ecosystem (प्रयुक्त तकनीकों का विश्लेषण)

Every technology in SupportDesk was chosen intentionally to solve specific enterprise requirements:

Technology & Version Role in SupportDesk Why We Chose It (Engineering Justification)
Java 17 LTS Core Programming Language Long-Term Support release offering enhanced JVM performance, Text Blocks for multiline JSON test fixtures, records for immutable DTOs, and pattern matching.

JSON Web Tokens (JWT)
`com.auth0:java-jwt`		 Stateless Authentication Allows stateless horizontal scaling without server-side HTTP session storage. Encodes user ID, email, role, and a cryptographic password fingerprint directly into claims.

`hibernate-validator`		 Input Validation Standardized declarative validation annotations (`@NotBlank`, `@Size`, `@Email`, `@Pattern`) that intercept invalid payloads before hitting service logic.
Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) Frontend Client Architecture Ultra-lightweight Single-Page Application without heavy node_modules dependencies. Manages sessions strictly in memory to eliminate cookie/storage vulnerabilities.

3.2 Application Entry Point (`SupportDeskApplication.java`)

SupportDeskApplication.javaJava 17 / Spring Boot
package com.supportdesk;

import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;

@SpringBootApplication
public class SupportDeskApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(SupportDeskApplication.class, args);
    }
}
How Spring Boot Starts (@SpringBootApplication का महत्व)
English: `@SpringBootApplication` is a convenience meta-annotation that bundles three vital annotations: 1. `@Configuration`: Marks the class as a source of bean definitions for the Spring Application Context. 2. `@EnableAutoConfiguration`: Tells Spring Boot to automatically configure beans based on classpath dependencies (e.g., configuring HikariCP DataSource because MySQL driver is present). 3. `@ComponentScan`: Scans `com.supportdesk` and all sub-packages for `@Component`, `@Service`, `@Repository`, and `@RestController` classes to instantiate them as Spring managed beans.
Hinglish: `@SpringBootApplication` तीन प्रमुख एनोटेशन्स का समूह है: `@Configuration` (बीन कॉन्फ़िगरेशन के लिए), `@EnableAutoConfiguration` (क्लासपाथ की जार फाइल्स देखकर स्वचालित सेटअप के लिए), और `@ComponentScan` (यह `com.supportdesk` के अंदर की सभी क्लासेज को स्कैन करके उनके ऑब्जेक्ट्स यानी स्प्रिंग बीन्स बनाता है)। जब `main` मेथड चलती है, तो यह एम्बेडेड टॉमकैट सर्वर शुरू करती है और एप्लिकेशन पोर्ट 8082 पर लाइव हो जाती है।

Chapter 4 — Application Architecture & Layered Flow

4.1 Layered Architecture Overview (स्तरीय वास्तुकला)

SupportDesk enforces a strict Separation of Concerns (SoC) through a 4-tier layered architecture:

Figure 4.1: SupportDesk 4-Tier Layered Architecture Diagram

4.2 End-to-End Request Execution Flow (अनुरोध निष्पादन प्रवाह)

When an employee clicks "Create Ticket", the request traverses through every layer as visualized below:

Figure 4.2: Step-by-Step Request Lifecycle from Browser to MySQL Database
Layer Primary Class / Component Responsibility in the Flow (प्रवाह में ज़िम्मेदारी)
1. Client / Browser `api.js` (Fetch API) Submits HTTP POST `/api/tickets` with JSON body and `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`.
2. Security Filter `JwtAuthenticationFilter.java` Extracts token, validates cryptographic signature, checks expiration, verifies password fingerprint (`pwd`), and populates `SecurityContext`.
3. REST Controller `TicketController.java` Validates input payload via `@Valid @RequestBody`, checks identity spoofing (`SecurityUtils`), and delegates to `TicketService`.
4. Service Layer `TicketService.java` Begins transaction (`@Transactional`), computes SLA deadline via `calculateSlaDeadline()`, generates unique ticket number, and calls repositories.
5. Data Access Layer `TicketRepository.java` Translates Java entity operations into parameterized SQL `INSERT` statements executed by Hibernate ORM engine.
6. Database Engine MySQL 8.0 (`supportdesk_db`) Executes atomic SQL statements, assigns auto-incremented primary key, and commits transaction.

Chapter 5 — Database Schema, ERD & SQL Queries

5.1 Relational Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD)

SupportDesk's database structure comprises five core tables linked via relational foreign key constraints:

Figure 5.1: Relational Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD)

5.2 Relational Tables Breakdown (टेबल्स का विस्तृत विवरण)

Table Name Primary Key Foreign Keys Business Purpose (व्यावसायिक उद्देश्य)
`employees` `id` (BIGINT AUTO) None Stores user credentials (BCrypt password hash), corporate email (Unique), department, active status, and RBAC role (`ADMIN`, `TECHNICIAN`, `EMPLOYEE`).
`tickets` `id` (BIGINT AUTO) `employee_id` → `employees(id)`
`assigned_technician_id` → `employees(id)`		 Stores ticket metadata, unique ticket number (`TCK-YYYYMMDD-XXXX`), status, priority, category, resolution notes, and SLA deadline timestamp.
`ticket_comments` `id` (BIGINT AUTO) `ticket_id` → `tickets(id)`
`employee_id` → `employees(id)`		 Stores threaded discussions, internal technician notes, and communications related to a specific ticket.
`ticket_activities` `id` (BIGINT AUTO) `ticket_id` → `tickets(id)`
`employee_id` → `employees(id)`		 Maintains an append-only, tamper-proof audit history recording every status change, technician assignment, and resolution event.
`notifications` `id` (BIGINT AUTO) `recipient_id` → `employees(id)`
`ticket_id` → `tickets(id)`		 Stores in-app alerts dispatched to users when their tickets are assigned, commented upon, or updated.

5.3 Why Entities and DTOs Are Strictly Separated (Entity बनाम DTO)

Architectural Principle: Entity vs DTO
English: In SupportDesk, JPA Entities (`Employee.java`, `Ticket.java`) represent the exact relational database tables. They are NEVER directly exposed as API request or response bodies. Instead, we use dedicated Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) like `CreateTicketRequest.java`, `UpdateEmployeeRequest.java`, and `LoginResponse.java`.

Key Reasons: 1. Security: Prevents Mass Assignment attacks (e.g., an employee sending `"role": "ADMIN"` in a profile update). 2. Credential Protection: Ensures passwords and BCrypt hashes are NEVER serialized into JSON output. 3. Decoupling: Allows database schemas to evolve independently without breaking frontend API contracts.
Hinglish: एंटिटी (Entity) और DTO को अलग रखना सॉफ्टवेयर आर्किटेक्चर का एक महत्वपूर्ण नियम है। एंटिटी सीधे डेटाबेस की टेबल से जुड़ी होती है। अगर हम एंटिटी को सीधे API में भेजेंगे, तो यूजर का पासवर्ड हैश गलती से JSON में लीक हो सकता है। DTO (Data Transfer Object) का उपयोग करके हम केवल वही डेटा क्लाइंट को भेजते हैं जिसकी उसे ज़रूरत होती है, जिससे हमारा एप्लिकेशन सुरक्षित और व्यवस्थित रहता है।

Chapter 6 — Employee Administration & Access Boundaries

6.1 Feature Overview & Business Rules (कर्मचारी प्रबंधन के नियम)

The Employee Administration subsystem manages corporate user identities, role assignments, department categorization, and soft-delete lifecycle operations.

Core Business Rules in EmployeeService (मुख्य व्यावसायिक नियम)
1. Duplicate Email Protection: Ensures corporate emails are globally unique. Throws `DuplicateEmailException` resulting in HTTP 409 Conflict. 2. Admin Lockout Safeguard: Prevents administrators from deactivating their own accounts or demoting themselves from `ADMIN` role. 3. Last Admin Protection: Prevents demoting or deactivating the last active administrator in the database. 4. Safe Password Updates: When updating an employee profile, if the password field is left null or blank (`""`), the existing encoded BCrypt hash is preserved intact. If a new password is provided, it is validated (≥ 6 characters) and re-encoded.
1. ईमेल की विशिष्टता (Unique Email): यदि कोई नया कर्मचारी पहले से मौजूद ईमेल से रजिस्टर करने की कोशिश करता है, तो सिस्टम `DuplicateEmailException` (HTTP 409) फेंकता है। 2. एडमिन सेल्फ-लॉकआउट से बचाव: एडमिनिस्ट्रेटर खुद के अकाउंट को डीएक्टिवेट (सस्पेंड) नहीं कर सकता और न ही अपने रोल को कम कर सकता है। 3. अंतिम एडमिन सुरक्षा: सिस्टम कंपनी के अंतिम सक्रिय एडमिन को डिलीट या डिमोट करने की अनुमति नहीं देता ताकि सिस्टम अनाथ (orphaned) न हो। 4. सुरक्षित पासवर्ड अपडेट: प्रोफ़ाइल एडिट करते समय यदि पासवर्ड खाली छोड़ा जाए, तो पुराना पासवर्ड हैश सुरक्षित रहता है; बदलने पर ही नया BCrypt हैश बनता है।

6.3 Critical Code Analysis (`EmployeeService.java`)

EmployeeService.javaLines 121–174
public Employee updateEmployee(Long id, UpdateEmployeeRequest updatedData) {
    if (updatedData == null) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Updated employee data cannot be null.");
    }

    Employee existing = getEmployeeById(id);

    // 1. Check duplicate email if changed
    String normalizedNewEmail = updatedData.getEmail() != null ? updatedData.getEmail().trim().toLowerCase() : "";
    if (!existing.getEmail().equalsIgnoreCase(normalizedNewEmail)) {
        if (employeeRepository.existsByEmail(normalizedNewEmail)) {
            throw new DuplicateEmailException("Email '" + updatedData.getEmail() + "' is already in use.");
        }
        existing.setEmail(normalizedNewEmail);
    }

    // 2. Prevent demoting the last active administrator or demoting oneself
    if (existing.getRole() == Role.ADMIN && updatedData.getRole() != null && updatedData.getRole() != Role.ADMIN && existing.isActive()) {
        Employee currentEmployee = securityUtils != null ? securityUtils.getCurrentEmployeeOrNull() : null;
        if (currentEmployee != null && currentEmployee.getId().equals(id)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Administrators cannot demote their own account from the ADMIN role.");
        }
        List<Employee> activeAdmins = employeeRepository.findActiveEmployeesByRoleForUpdate(Role.ADMIN);
        if (activeAdmins.size() <= 1) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Cannot demote the last active administrator account.");
        }
    }

    if (updatedData.getName() != null) existing.setName(updatedData.getName().trim());
    if (updatedData.getDepartment() != null) existing.setDepartment(updatedData.getDepartment().trim());
    if (updatedData.getRole() != null) existing.setRole(updatedData.getRole());

    // 3. Preserve password if blank; encode only if valid new password is provided
    if (updatedData.getPassword() != null && !updatedData.getPassword().isBlank()) {
        String rawPassword = updatedData.getPassword().trim();
        if (rawPassword.length() < 6) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Password must be at least 6 characters.");
        }
        existing.setPassword(passwordEncoder.encode(rawPassword));
    }

    return employeeRepository.save(existing);
}
Code LineTechnical Explanation (तकनीकी व्याख्या)
if (!existing.getEmail().equalsIgnoreCase(...)) Checks if the user is attempting to modify their email address. If modified, queries `existsByEmail()` to prevent duplicate registrations across tenants.
if (currentEmployee.getId().equals(id)) Checks if the currently authenticated user in `SecurityContextHolder` is attempting to demote themselves from `ADMIN` to `EMPLOYEE`, which would cause self-lockout.
if (activeAdmins.size() <= 1) Locks the admin role if only one administrator remains active in the company, maintaining governance continuity.
if (updatedData.getPassword() != null && !blank) Solves the classic beginner bug where updating an employee's phone number accidentally wipes out or overwrites their encrypted password hash with null.

7.3 Critical Code Analysis: Technician Assignment (`TicketService.java`)

TicketService.javaTechnician Assignment with Proper Actor Attribution
@Transactional
public Ticket assignTechnician(Long ticketId, Long technicianId, Employee performingActor) {
    Ticket ticket = getTicketById(ticketId);
    Employee technician = employeeService.getEmployeeById(technicianId);

    // Enforce business constraint: Assignee must hold TECHNICIAN role
    if (technician.getRole() != Role.TECHNICIAN) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee " + technician.getName() + " does not have the TECHNICIAN role.");
    }

    ticket.setAssignedTechnician(technician);
    ticket.setStatus(TicketStatus.ASSIGNED);
    Ticket savedTicket = ticketRepository.save(ticket);

    // Audit Logging: Record the authenticated administrator as the actor, NOT the technician
    Employee actor = performingActor != null ? performingActor : technician;
    logActivity(
        savedTicket,
        actor,
        ActivityType.TECHNICIAN_ASSIGNED,
        "Ticket assigned to technician " + technician.getName()
    );

    // Dispatch in-app notification to technician
    notificationService.createNotification(
        technician,
        savedTicket,
        "New Ticket Assigned",
        "You have been assigned ticket: " + savedTicket.getTicketNumber(),
        NotificationType.TICKET_ASSIGNED
    );

    return savedTicket;
}

Chapter 8 — Priority-Based SLA & Overdue Detection Engine

8.1 What is an SLA and Why Does It Matter? (SLA क्या है?)

Service Level Agreement (SLA) Fundamentals
English: A Service Level Agreement (SLA) is a contractual resolution commitment between IT support and business operations. In SupportDesk, every ticket has an automated countdown deadline calculated at the exact moment of ticket creation based on its severity priority.
Hinglish: SLA (सर्विस लेवल एग्रीमेंट) का मतलब है कि किसी समस्या को हल करने में आईटी टीम अधिकतम कितना समय लेगी। उदाहरण के लिए, यदि कंपनी का मुख्य डेटाबेस या बिलिंग सिस्टम बंद हो गया (CRITICAL), तो उसे 4 घंटे में ठीक करना अनिवार्य है। यदि किसी को नया माउस चाहिए (LOW), तो उसके लिए 48 घंटे का समय होता है।

8.2 Priority Tiers & Rules (प्राथमिकता श्रेणियाँ)

Priority SLA Hours Config Property Criteria & Example
CRITICAL 4 Hours `app.sla.critical-hours=4` Production outage, server down, ERP unavailable, security breach.
HIGH 8 Hours `app.sla.high-hours=8` Department-level blocker without immediate workaround (VPN gateway failure).
MEDIUM 24 Hours `app.sla.medium-hours=24` Single user operational issue (printer malfunction, email sync lag).
LOW 48 Hours `app.sla.low-hours=48` Non-blocking queries, software upgrade requests, peripheral replacement.

8.4 Overdue Detection Query (`TicketRepository.java`)

TicketRepository.javaJPQL Overdue Query
@Query("SELECT t FROM Ticket t WHERE t.slaDeadline < :now AND t.status NOT IN " +
       "(com.supportdesk.entity.TicketStatus.RESOLVED, com.supportdesk.entity.TicketStatus.CLOSED) " +
       "ORDER BY t.slaDeadline ASC")
List<Ticket> findOverdueTickets(@Param("now") LocalDateTime now);

Crucial Business Logic: Even if a ticket's deadline timestamp has passed, if the ticket status is `RESOLVED` or `CLOSED`, it is NEVER marked as overdue! This is thoroughly validated in `TicketServiceTests.testResolvedTicketNotOverdue()`.

9.1 Authentication Flow & Token Revocation Architecture

SupportDesk employs stateless JSON Web Tokens signed with HMAC-SHA256. To solve the vulnerability where stolen tokens remain valid after a password reset, SupportDesk embeds an HMAC-SHA256 Password Fingerprint (`pwd` claim) in every token:

Figure 9.1: Stateless JWT Authentication & Instant Password Revocation Architecture

9.3 Critical Code Analysis: Password Fingerprint (`JwtUtil.java`)

JwtUtil.javaStateless Password Fingerprinting
public String computePasswordFingerprint(String passwordHash) {
    if (passwordHash == null || passwordHash.isBlank()) return "";
    try {
        javax.crypto.Mac mac = javax.crypto.Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA256");
        javax.crypto.spec.SecretKeySpec secretKeySpec =
                new javax.crypto.spec.SecretKeySpec(secret.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8), "HmacSHA256");
        mac.init(secretKeySpec);
        byte[] hmac = mac.doFinal(passwordHash.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
        return HexFormat.of().formatHex(hmac).substring(0, 32);
    } catch (Exception ex) {
        return "";
    }
}

public boolean isTokenValidForPassword(String token, String currentPasswordHash) {
    try {
        DecodedJWT decoded = validateToken(token);
        String tokenPwdClaim = decoded.getClaim("pwd").asString();
        if (tokenPwdClaim != null && !tokenPwdClaim.isBlank()) {
            String currentFingerprint = computePasswordFingerprint(currentPasswordHash);
            return tokenPwdClaim.equals(currentFingerprint);
        }
        return true;
    } catch (JWTVerificationException ex) {
        return false;
    }
}

Chapter 11 — Frontend SPA Architecture & API Integration

11.1 The In-Memory Session Architecture (`auth.js`)

Modern web security best practices strongly advise against storing sensitive bearer tokens in browser `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` due to vulnerability to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) extraction attacks. SupportDesk implements a secure In-Memory Closure Pattern:

auth.jsIn-Memory Private Closure
const AuthService = (function() {
    // Private in-memory variables protected inside closure
    let _token = null;
    let _user = null;

    return {
        getToken() { return _token; },
        setToken(token) { _token = token; },
        getUser() { return _user; },
        setUser(user) { _user = user; },
        isAuthenticated() { return Boolean(_token && _user); },
        clear() { _token = null; _user = null; }
    };
})();

12.2 Critical Code Analysis: Data Leakage Protection (`GlobalExceptionHandler.java`)

GlobalExceptionHandler.javaDefensive Sanitization
@ExceptionHandler(DataIntegrityViolationException.class)
public ResponseEntity<Map<String, Object>> handleDataIntegrityViolation(DataIntegrityViolationException ex) {
    // Server logs the real SQL and constraint error for engineers
    logger.error("Database constraint violation occurred: ", ex);
    // Client receives sanitized error without leaking SQL table or column details
    return buildErrorResponse(
        HttpStatus.CONFLICT,
        "Database constraint violation: The operation could not be completed due to conflicting data."
    );
}

@ExceptionHandler(Exception.class)
public ResponseEntity<Map<String, Object>> handleGeneralException(Exception ex) {
    logger.error("Unhandled server exception encountered: ", ex);
    return buildErrorResponse(
        HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
        "An unexpected internal server error occurred. Please contact support or try again later."
    );
}

Chapter 15 — Production Troubleshooting & Debugging

Observed IssueConfirmed Root CauseResolution Step
HTTP 401 vs 403 Confusion 401 means "Unauthenticated" (missing or expired JWT); 403 means "Forbidden" (authenticated, but lacking required role). Provide valid credentials in `POST /api/auth/login` for 401; verify role permissions in `SecurityConfig` for 403.
CORS Cross-Origin Failure Frontend running on different port (e.g. 3000) not listed in `app.cors.allowed-origins`. Add origin to `application.properties` or supply `APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` environment variable.
Token Suddenly Invalidated The user's password was changed, triggering HMAC fingerprint mismatch in `JwtAuthenticationFilter`. Expected security behavior: Re-authenticate with new password to receive fresh token.
Database Connection Refused MySQL service is stopped or port 3306 is blocked. Verify MySQL status in Windows Services or run `Start-Service MySQL80`.

Chapter 16 — Technical Limitations & Future Roadmap

Truthful Architectural Audit (सच्ची तकनीकी समीक्षा)
Current Limitations: 1. Database Migrations: Currently uses Hibernate `update` in dev and `validate` in prod. Recommended upgrade: Flyway or Liquibase for versioned SQL migrations. 2. Real-time Updates: In-app notifications rely on client-side polling rather than WebSocket/STOMP push. 3. Distributed Token Blacklist: The HMAC password fingerprint invalidates tokens on password change, but explicit single-device logout relies on client-side token deletion. Multi-node distributed logout could benefit from Redis. 4. Cloud Deployment: Tested locally and container-ready; not currently deployed to a cloud cluster (AWS/GCP).
Hinglish: एक ईमानदार डेवलपर इंटरव्यू में कभी झूठे दावे नहीं करता। हमारे प्रोजेक्ट में ये वास्तविक सीमाएँ हैं: अभी इसमें डेटाबेस माइग्रेशन टूल (Flyway) नहीं है, रीयल-टाइम अपडेट्स के लिए WebSocket के बजाय पोलिंग है, और यह लोकल सर्वर पर पूरी तरह टेस्टेड है पर एडब्ल्यूएस/क्लाउड पर डिप्लॉयड नहीं है। भविष्य में इन्हें अपग्रेड किया जा सकता है।

Chapter 17 — Core Technical Interview Questions & Answers

Here are the 25 most critical interview questions regarding SupportDesk with model answers in both English and Hinglish:

Q1. What is SupportDesk and what architectural problems did it solve?Core Architecture
English Answer: "SupportDesk is an IT help desk ticketing system built with Java 17, Spring Boot, Spring Security, and MySQL. It replaced ad-hoc email communications with a formal state-machine ticket lifecycle (`OPEN` → `ASSIGNED` → `IN_PROGRESS` → `RESOLVED` → `CLOSED`), an automated 4-tier SLA countdown engine, and strict role-based access control. Key architectural challenges solved include identity spoofing prevention, zero sensitive data leakage in JSON, and stateless JWT revocation upon password changes."
Hinglish Explanation: "SupportDesk ईमेल के ज़रिए होने वाली अव्यवस्था को हल करता है। यह टिकट्स का एक निश्चित जीवनचक्र तय करता है, प्राथमिकता अनुसार 4 घंटे से 48 घंटे की SLA समयसीमा निर्धारित करता है, और रोल-बेस्ड सुरक्षा लागू करता है ताकि कर्मचारी केवल अपनी टिकट देख सकें और एडमिन पूरा सिस्टम प्रबंधित कर सकें।"
Relevant Classes: `TicketService.java`, `SecurityConfig.java` | Confirmed tested: 185 tests
Q2. How is authentication implemented, and how are JWTs verified on each request?Security
English Answer: "Authentication is stateless using JSON Web Tokens signed with HMAC-SHA256 (`app.jwt.secret`). When a user submits credentials to `POST /api/auth/login`, `AuthService` verifies the BCrypt hash against the database and calls `JwtUtil.generateToken()`. On each subsequent request, `JwtAuthenticationFilter` intercepts the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, verifies the cryptographic signature, checks token expiration, confirms the password fingerprint matches the current DB hash, and loads the user into Spring Security's `SecurityContextHolder`."
Hinglish Explanation: "लॉगिन पर स्प्रिंग सिक्योरिटी पासवर्ड का BCrypt हैश चेक करती है और सही होने पर एक JWT टोकन देती है। हर अगले अनुरोध पर `JwtAuthenticationFilter` टोकन का सिग्नेचर, एक्सपायरी और पासवर्ड फिंगरप्रिंट चेक करके यूजर को ऑथेंटिकेट करता है।"
Relevant Classes: `JwtUtil.java`, `JwtAuthenticationFilter.java`, `AuthService.java`
Q3. How did you solve the problem of invalidating JWTs after a password change without a database table?Advanced Security
English Answer: "Because JWTs are stateless, changing a user's password usually leaves existing active tokens valid until expiry. Rather than introducing a heavy database session table or distributed cache (Redis) that would break production `ddl-auto=validate`, I implemented a Stateless HMAC-SHA256 Password Fingerprint. In `JwtUtil`, when a token is issued, we compute a one-way HMAC-SHA256 hash of the employee's current BCrypt password hash and embed it as a `pwd` claim. When the user changes their password, a new BCrypt hash is generated. On subsequent requests, `JwtAuthenticationFilter` compares the token's `pwd` claim against the HMAC of the current DB hash; the mismatch causes immediate rejection (HTTP 401)."
Hinglish Explanation: "यह एक बहुत प्रभावशाली उत्तर है। सामान्यतः JWT स्टेटलेस होने के कारण पासवर्ड बदलने पर भी 24 घंटे तक चलता रहता है। मैंने बिना किसी नई डेटाबेस टेबल के, यूजर के पासवर्ड हैश का एक सुरक्षित HMAC फिंगरप्रिंट टोकन के अंदर `pwd` क्लेम में रख दिया। जब पासवर्ड बदलता है, तो नया हैश बनता है और पुराना टोकन तुरंत अमान्य (401) हो जाता है।"
Relevant Classes: `JwtUtil.computePasswordFingerprint()`, `JwtAuthenticationFilter.doFilterInternal()`
Q4. How does the SLA calculation engine work?Business Logic
English Answer: "The SLA engine is implemented in `TicketService.calculateSlaDeadline()`. When a ticket is created, its priority determines the resolution target: CRITICAL is 4 hours, HIGH is 8 hours, MEDIUM is 24 hours, and LOW is 48 hours. The deadline timestamp (`slaDeadline`) is computed by adding these hours to `LocalDateTime.now()` and stored in the `tickets` table. To find overdue tickets, `TicketRepository.findOverdueTickets()` queries all tickets where `slaDeadline < :now` and the status is neither `RESOLVED` nor `CLOSED`."
Hinglish Explanation: "टिकट बनते समय ही उसकी प्राथमिकता के आधार पर डेडलाइन तय हो जाती है (जैसे CRITICAL के लिए 4 घंटे)। डेटाबेस में यह समय सेव होता है। यदि समय बीत जाए और टिकट हल न हुआ हो, तो वह 'Overdue' की श्रेणी में आ जाता है।"
Relevant Classes: `TicketService.java`, `TicketRepository.java`
Q5. How do you prevent identity spoofing in ticket creation and commenting?RBAC / Security
English Answer: "In `TicketController.java`, when an employee submits a ticket or posts a comment with an `employeeId` in the request body, the controller cross-verifies that ID against `securityUtils.getCurrentEmployee()`. If a non-admin user attempts to submit a ticket or comment under someone else's ID, the request is immediately rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden: 'Identity spoofing rejected: You cannot create tickets on behalf of another employee.'"
Hinglish Explanation: "अगर कोई चालाक यूजर JSON रिक्वेस्ट बॉडी में किसी दूसरे कर्मचारी की ID भेजकर टिकट या कमेंट दर्ज करना चाहे, तो हमारा कंट्रोलर टोकन के अंदर मौजूद असली यूजर ID से उसकी तुलना करता है और मिसमैच होने पर 403 Forbidden एरर देता है।"
Tested in: `SecurityAccessAndRbacTests.testIdentitySpoofingCreateTicketRejected()`
Q6. Why did you use `@RestControllerAdvice` and how does it prevent information leakage?Architecture
English Answer: "`GlobalExceptionHandler.java` uses `@RestControllerAdvice` to intercept exceptions across all controllers. For example, if a `DataIntegrityViolationException` occurs, we log the SQL details internally on the server, but return a sanitized client message: 'Database constraint violation: The operation could not be completed due to conflicting data.' This prevents database table names, column constraints, SQL syntax, or internal file paths from ever leaking to external clients."
Hinglish Explanation: "ग्लोबल एक्सेप्शन हैंडलर पूरे एप्लिकेशन की गलतियों को पकड़ता है। प्रोडक्शन में कभी भी स्क्रीन पर SQL एरर या जावा का स्टैक ट्रेस नहीं दिखना चाहिए। हम सर्वर लॉग में असली एरर लिखते हैं, लेकिन यूजर को सिर्फ साफ़ और सुरक्षित संदेश (जैसे Bad Request, Conflict) भेजते हैं।"
Relevant Classes: `GlobalExceptionHandler.java`
Q7. What is the difference between JPA and Hibernate in this project?Fundamentals
English Answer: "JPA (Jakarta Persistence API) is a specification/interface that defines how Java objects map to relational databases. Hibernate is the actual underlying implementation (the engine) that does the heavy lifting. In SupportDesk, we use Spring Data JPA repository interfaces, and Hibernate 7 automatically generates the SQL queries behind the scenes."
Hinglish Explanation: "JPA एक नियम पुस्तिका (इंटेरफ़ेस) है, जबकि हाइबरनेट (Hibernate) उस नियम पर काम करने वाला वास्तविक सॉफ्टवेयर (इंजन) है। हम कोड में JPA एनोटेशन्स (`@Entity`, `@ManyToOne`) लिखते हैं, और हाइबरनेट उन्हें SQL में बदलता है।"
Dependencies: `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa`, `hibernate-core 7.4.5`
Q8. How does the employee update process avoid overwriting existing password hashes?Service Logic
English Answer: "In `EmployeeService.updateEmployee()`, we check if the updated data's password is non-null and not blank. If the administrator only updates the employee's department or phone number, leaving the password blank, the existing encoded BCrypt hash in `existing.getPassword()` is left completely untouched. A new BCrypt hash is only computed if a valid password of 6 or more characters is provided."
Hinglish Explanation: "अगर प्रोफ़ाइल एडिट करते समय पासवर्ड फील्ड खाली हो, तो कोड पुराने पासवर्ड हैश को वैसा ही छोड़ देता है। केवल तभी नया BCrypt हैश बनता है जब यूजर कम से कम 6 अक्षरों का नया पासवर्ड भरे।"
Tested in: `EmployeeServiceTests.testUpdateEmployeeProfileOnlyPreservesPasswordHash()`
Q9. What is the N+1 problem, and how was it avoided in the dashboard?Database Performance
English Answer: "The N+1 problem occurs when an application executes 1 initial query to fetch N parent records, and then executes N separate queries to fetch related child records. In `DashboardService.java`, technician workload calculations previously threatened an N+1 pattern if technicians were queried in a loop. We optimized this using single aggregated queries (`countPendingByTechnicianId`, `countResolvedByTechnicianId`) and direct database count queries (`countByStatus`, `countOverdueTickets`), executing aggregations directly on MySQL."
Hinglish Explanation: "N+1 समस्या तब होती है जब डेटाबेस पर लूप चलाकर बार-बार क्वेरी भेजी जाती है। हमने डैशबोर्ड में लूप क्वेरी के बजाय सीधे MySQL से काउंट और एग्रीगेशन क्वेरीज़ चलाईं, जिससे डेटाबेस का लोड बहुत कम हो गया।"
Relevant Classes: `DashboardService.java`, `TicketRepository.java`
Q10. What is the role of `SecurityContextHolder` in Spring Security?Spring Security
English Answer: "`SecurityContextHolder` is where Spring Security stores details of the currently authenticated principal using a `ThreadLocal` storage strategy. In `JwtAuthenticationFilter`, once the JWT is validated, we construct a `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken` containing the user's `UserDetails` and authorities (`ROLE_ADMIN`, `ROLE_TECHNICIAN`, `ROLE_EMPLOYEE`) and set it into `SecurityContextHolder.getContext().setAuthentication(...)`."
Hinglish Explanation: "`SecurityContextHolder` एक थ्रेड-लोकल मेमोरी बॉक्स है जहाँ स्प्रिंग सिक्योरिटी वर्तमान में लॉग-इन यूजर की जानकारी और उसके रोल रखती है। कंट्रोलर में कहीं भी `SecurityContextHolder` से पता चल जाता है कि वर्तमान यूजर कौन है।"
Relevant Classes: `JwtAuthenticationFilter.java`, `SecurityUtils.java`

Chapter 18 — Practical Mock Interview: 80 Questions Bank

This chapter provides an exhaustive repository of 80 categorized questions: 30 Beginner, 30 Intermediate, and 20 Advanced questions with concise model answers.

Section A: 30 Beginner-Level Questions & Answers

#Beginner QuestionModel Answer (English + Hinglish)
1What is Spring Boot?An opinionated framework that simplifies Spring development by providing auto-configuration and embedded servers (स्प्रिंग डेवलपमेंट को आसान बनाने वाला टूल).
2What is Maven?A build automation and dependency management tool using `pom.xml` (लाइब्रेरी और बिल्ड मैनेज करने वाला टूल).
3What port does SupportDesk run on?Port 8082, configured in `application.properties` via `server.port=8082`.
4What is `@RestController`?A combination of `@Controller` and `@ResponseBody`, returning JSON directly (डेटा को JSON में रिटर्न करने वाला कंट्रोलर).
5What is `@Autowired`?Enables automatic dependency injection by Spring's IoC container (ऑब्जेक्ट को ऑटोमैटिक इंजेक्ट करना).
6What is an Entity in JPA?A Java class mapped to a database table via `@Entity` (डेटाबेस टेबल का जावा रूप).
7What is `@Table` annotation?Specifies the exact table name in the relational database (टेबल का नाम तय करना).
8What is `@Id` and `@GeneratedValue`?Defines the primary key and its generation strategy, like `GenerationType.IDENTITY` (प्राइमरी की और ऑटो-इंक्रीमेंट).
9What is a DTO?Data Transfer Object: carries data between client and server without exposing entity structures.
10What is BCrypt?A salted password hashing function that is computationally resistant to brute-force attacks (पासवर्ड को सुरक्षित एनक्रिप्ट करने वाला अल्गोरिदम).
11What is the difference between GET and POST?GET retrieves data safely without side-effects; POST creates a new resource on the server.
12What is the purpose of PUT vs PATCH?PUT replaces a resource completely; PATCH applies partial modifications.
13What does HTTP 201 Created mean?The request succeeded and led to the creation of a new resource (e.g., ticket created).
14What does HTTP 400 Bad Request mean?Client sent malformed data or violated Bean Validation constraints.
15What does HTTP 401 Unauthorized mean?Authentication is missing, token expired, or invalid credentials provided.
16What does HTTP 403 Forbidden mean?User is authenticated, but lacks permission for that specific endpoint.
17What does HTTP 404 Not Found mean?The requested resource ID or URL does not exist.
18What does HTTP 409 Conflict mean?Conflict with current database state (e.g. duplicate email registration).
19What does HTTP 500 mean?Internal server error: unhandled exception caught by global handler.
20What is an Enum in Java?A special data type representing a fixed set of constants (`Role`, `TicketStatus`, `TicketPriority`).
21What are the three roles in SupportDesk?`ADMIN`, `TECHNICIAN`, and `EMPLOYEE`.
22What are the 5 ticket statuses?`OPEN`, `ASSIGNED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `RESOLVED`, `CLOSED`.
23What are the 4 priorities?`CRITICAL` (4h), `HIGH` (8h), `MEDIUM` (24h), `LOW` (48h).
24What does `@Transactional` do?Ensures all database operations inside the method either complete fully or roll back completely.
25What is `JpaRepository`?Spring Data interface providing CRUD operations (`save`, `findById`, `findAll`, `delete`).
26What is Bean Validation?Standard declarative annotations like `@NotBlank`, `@Size`, `@Email` to validate inputs.
27What is MockMvc?Spring test utility that simulates HTTP requests to controllers without starting a real server.
28What database is used?MySQL 8.0 on port 3306 with database name `supportdesk_db`.
29Where is the application entry point?`SupportDeskApplication.java` in package `com.supportdesk`.
30How many automated tests exist?185 passing tests with zero errors and zero failures.

Section B: 30 Intermediate-Level Questions & Answers

#Intermediate QuestionModel Answer (English + Hinglish)
31How does `JwtAuthenticationFilter` intercept requests?Extends `OncePerRequestFilter`, checks `Authorization: Bearer` header, validates token signature and expiry.
32What is the difference between `@Component`, `@Service`, and `@Repository`?All are Spring beans; `@Service` designates business logic; `@Repository` handles data access with exception translation.
33How is CORS handled in SupportDesk?Configured in `SecurityConfig.java` reading trusted origins from `app.cors.allowed-origins` property.
34Why is CSRF disabled in `SecurityConfig`?Because authentication is stateless via Bearer JWTs without cookie-based session tracking.
35What is `SecurityUtils`?A helper component that extracts the currently authenticated `Employee` from `SecurityContextHolder`.
36How does the ticket number get formatted?Format `TCK-YYYYMMDD-XXXX` using current date and a 6-character unique hex or alphanumeric string.
37What happens if an inactive employee tries to log in?`CustomUserDetailsService` loads `UserPrincipal` with `isEnabled()=false`, throwing `DisabledException`/`BadCredentialsException` (HTTP 401).
38What happens if an inactive employee tries to create a ticket?`TicketService.createTicket()` checks `creator.isActive()`; if false, throws `IllegalArgumentException` (HTTP 400).
39Can a regular EMPLOYEE view other employees' tickets?No. In `TicketController.getAllTickets()`, non-admin, non-technician users only receive tickets where `employee.id == currentUser.id`.
40Can an EMPLOYEE assign a technician?No. Endpoint `/api/tickets/{id}/assign` requires the `ADMIN` role. Regular employees receive 403 Forbidden.
41Can an EMPLOYEE update a ticket status to RESOLVED?No. Only `ADMIN` and `TECHNICIAN` can update status or submit resolution notes.
42What happens if an admin tries to assign a non-technician employee?`TicketService` checks `technician.getRole() == Role.TECHNICIAN`; if false, throws HTTP 400 Bad Request.
43Who is recorded as the actor in technician assignment?The authenticated administrator who executed the assignment, while the technician is recorded as the target.
44How are notifications generated?`NotificationService.createNotification()` saves a record in `notifications` table linked to the recipient.
45How does the frontend know which tabs to show?`app.js` inspects `AuthService.getUser().role` and toggles DOM visibility for admin and technician controls.
46Where is the JWT token stored on the frontend?In a private JavaScript closure variable inside `auth.js`, never in `localStorage` or cookies.
47What happens when the browser page is refreshed?In-memory state resets, prompting the user to sign in again cleanly.
48What is a derived query in Spring Data JPA?A query generated by Spring from method names, like `findByPriority(TicketPriority p)`.
49What is JPQL?Java Persistence Query Language: queries entities and their fields rather than raw database tables.
50How does `GlobalExceptionHandler` format field errors?Collects all `FieldError` items from `BindingResult` into a `Map<String, String> validationErrors`.
51What is the purpose of `CustomAuthenticationEntryPoint`?Intercepts unauthenticated requests at the filter boundary and returns uniform JSON with status 401.
52What is the purpose of `CustomAccessDeniedHandler`?Intercepts unauthorized requests (authenticated but lacking role) and returns uniform JSON with status 403.
53How do you verify passwords match in BCrypt?Using `passwordEncoder.matches(rawPassword, encodedHash)`.
54Can two employees share the same email?No. `existsByEmail()` check enforces uniqueness, throwing `DuplicateEmailException` (HTTP 409).
55Can an admin deactivate themselves?No. `EmployeeService` explicitly prohibits admin self-deactivation to prevent accidental lockout.
56Can an admin demote themselves from ADMIN to EMPLOYEE?No. `EmployeeService` rejects self-demotion with an `IllegalArgumentException`.
57How are activity logs sorted?Chronologically ascending by `createdAt` so history reads from creation to resolution.
58How are comments sorted?Chronologically ascending by `createdAt` to display conversation flow.
59What is HikariCP?High-performance JDBC connection pool used by default in Spring Boot.
60How does `@Transactional` handle exceptions?By default, it rolls back for unchecked exceptions (`RuntimeException` and `Error`).

Section C: 20 Advanced-Level Questions & Answers

#Advanced QuestionModel Answer (English + Hinglish)
61Explain the HMAC password fingerprint revocation mechanism.Generates HMAC-SHA256 of the user's BCrypt hash and stores it in token claim `pwd`. A password change produces a new hash, causing fingerprint mismatch and immediate token rejection.
62Why not use a Redis token blacklist instead?Redis adds infrastructure overhead and distributed state. The HMAC fingerprint is 100% stateless and requires zero database migrations or external cache services.
63What are the limitations of the HMAC password fingerprint?It revokes all previous tokens upon password change, but does not support selective single-device logout.
64How do you handle SQL injection prevention in SupportDesk?Spring Data JPA and Hibernate use JDBC prepared statements with parameterized inputs for all queries.
65How does the overdue query perform at scale?`findOverdueTickets` filters by `slaDeadline < :now` and indexed `status` column, avoiding full table scans.
66Why use Text Blocks in Spring Boot tests?Text Blocks (`"""`) provide readable multiline JSON payloads directly in test methods without escaping quotes.
67How does `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` optimize performance?Informs Hibernate not to track dirty entities for flush checks, reducing memory and CPU overhead.
68Explain Spring Security's `SecurityFilterChain` bean.Configures `HttpSecurity` rules, disabling CSRF, setting `SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS`, and registering `JwtAuthenticationFilter`.
69How does `UserPrincipal` bridge Employee and Spring Security?Implements `UserDetails`, mapping `Employee.getEmail()` to username and `Employee.getRole()` to `GrantedAuthority`.
70What is the difference between Unit Tests and Integration Tests in your suite?Unit tests (`TicketServiceTests`) test business logic in isolation; Integration tests (`SecurityAccessAndRbacTests`) use MockMvc with full Spring application context.
71How do you prevent Mass Assignment attacks?By never binding request payloads directly to entities; request DTOs strictly define permissible fields.
72How do you prevent XSS attacks in SupportDesk?Tokens are stored in private closure memory, and the frontend dynamically sets text using `.textContent` rather than raw `.innerHTML`.
73Why does `application-prod.properties` use `ddl-auto=validate`?To prevent Hibernate from altering production database schemas dynamically at runtime, ensuring DBA schema governance.
74How would you scale SupportDesk horizontally?Because authentication is stateless (JWT + HMAC fingerprint), multiple backend instances can sit behind a load balancer without sticky sessions.
75How would you migrate to WebSocket for real-time notifications?Add `spring-boot-starter-websocket`, configure a STOMP broker, and publish events via `SimpMessagingTemplate` in `NotificationService`.
76What is the difference between pessimistic and optimistic locking?Optimistic locking uses a `@Version` column; pessimistic locking uses database row locks (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`).
77Where is pessimistic locking used in SupportDesk?In `EmployeeRepository.findActiveEmployeesByRoleForUpdate(Role.ADMIN)` to prevent race conditions during admin demotions.
78What happens if two admins assign the same ticket simultaneously?The last transaction to commit updates the assigned technician and logs an activity entry; database integrity is maintained.
79How is password security verified in tests?`jsonPath("$.employee", not(hasKey("password")))` explicitly tests that passwords and hashes are never serialized into responses.
80What was your personal proudest technical accomplishment in this project?Devising and verifying the stateless HMAC password revocation mechanism that solved a critical security gap with zero database schema changes.

Appendix & Technical Terms Glossary

Key Technical Terminology (शब्दावली)

Glossary of Core Engineering Terms
  • Stateless: An architecture where the server retains no client session data between requests. Every request must carry all authentication credentials (e.g., Bearer JWT).
  • RBAC (Role-Based Access Control): Restricting system access to authorized users based on their assigned corporate roles (`ADMIN`, `TECHNICIAN`, `EMPLOYEE`).
  • BCrypt: An adaptive cryptographic hash function based on the Blowfish cipher incorporating salting and work factor iterations to defend against hardware brute-forcing.
  • HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code): A cryptographic construction using a secret key and a hash function (SHA-256) to verify data integrity and authenticity.
  • SLA (Service Level Agreement): A defined time commitment for resolving technical support requests based on issue severity.
  • MockMvc: Part of the Spring Test framework providing support for testing Spring MVC controllers with mocked HTTP requests and response assertions.
  • Idempotent: An operation that produces the exact same state even if executed multiple times (e.g., `PUT`, `DELETE`, or seeding existing database accounts).
